subject.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle

question: Should OpenClaw adopt resetSessionEntryLifecycle as a permanent public Plugin SDK contract for provider-observed external lifecycle boundaries?
rationale: The Teams fix is well-proven, but repository policy treats a new public Plugin SDK callable and its owner-handoff semantics as a durable compatibility decision that automation cannot approve.

options.title: Sponsor the SDK contract
options.body: Approve the generic fenced reset operation and its owner-coordinated harness handoff as the supported plugin lifecycle boundary, then merge the reviewed implementation.

options.title: Keep the reset internal
options.body: Refactor the operation behind a core-private or bundled-only seam and expose a narrower Teams capability instead of publishing the general callable.

options.title: Decline lifecycle resets
options.body: Close the PR and accept retained Teams context after reinstall until another existing core session boundary can safely express the behavior.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the SDK contract
recommendation.body: Approve the generic fenced reset operation and its owner-coordinated harness handoff as the supported plugin lifecycle boundary, then merge the reviewed implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the safety-scoping commit and are the clearest engaged owner for the Teams/core Plugin SDK boundary.
